These Banana Bread Muffins go CRAZY!! They’re super easy to make, super healthy, higher in protein and come out SO FIRE🙌
.
Full Recipe👇
Wet ingredients:
- mash 3 ripe bananas
- 2 whole eggs
- 3/4 cup Greek yogurt
- 2 tbsp maple
- 1 tsp vanilla
Dry Ingredients:
- 1.75 cups oat flour
- 2 scoops vanilla protein
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 2 tsp cinnamon
Assemble:
- mix wet ingredients
- add in dry ingredients and mix
- fold in dark chocolate chips(I did ~1/4 cup)
- add to a muffin tin
- bake at 350F for 15-20 mins
Macros: 160 cals | 9P | 24C | 4F(12 total muffins)
ENJOY!!
.
👨‍🍳Comment “RECIPE” for my full cookbook🙌
.

items.transcript: Might just be your new favorite healthy treat. Oh my gosh. Let's make my high protein banana bread muffins. To start, peel and add three bananas into a bowl and mash them. Add 2 eggs, three fourths cup of yogurt, a drizzle of maple syrup, a teaspoon of vanilla, then whisk before adding in oat flour, protein powder, and cinnamon. Now whisk again, fold in dark chocolate chips, transfer the batter into a muffin tin. If you have some butter left over, go for it. Once your oven hits three seventy-five, bake your muffins, squeak the tops to turn golden brown then pull them, plate them, and bang. High protein banana bread muffins.

items.caption:
Probiotic Mango Soda — using just the pits, peels, and water!

You can create a super healthy, refreshing, naturally bubbly soda with things most people would throw into the trash can! So yes, this is a free product to make and it’s super beneficial for you too. And, it’s also the most delicious thing ever!

I fermented mango peels, mango pits, in water for 6 days. Next I strained it and added in some coconut sugar. The coconut sugar is there solely to feed the yeast and produce CO2 during the second ferment. I bottle the mango soda with the sugar in airtight bottles and allow to further ferment until super bubbly, then I move the sodas to the fridge!

You can do this with most any fruit! Ill be posting a more detailed how-to on my site in the coming days, so stay tuned. But until then let me know if you have any questions!
items.transcript: We just finished the first ferment. These fermented for six days. It's got like a nice fermented mango smell. Pour this back into my jar. See how much I have. Take a little more than half a gallon and now I'm going to add some coconut sugar about three tablespoons during the second ferment. The yeast actually needs the sugar to produce COtwo. So without this, it would not get bubbly and it's not going to be sweet when it's done. It's literally going to use that sugar to create COtwo. Mango spritz

CMC’s dad didn’t even crack a smile 😂

Christian McCaffrey grew up following an unusually strict routine established by his father, Ed McCaffrey, a former NFL wide receiver and three-time Super Bowl champion.

According to Christian, the household rules and training included:

7:30 p.m. bedtime. No soda. Dynamic warmups. Strict phone rules: His parents confiscated their phones at night, and the boys weren’t allowed to have their own phones until eighth grade. Punishment for being tackled: Christian recalled that his father would ground him if an opponent tackled him by grabbing his jersey when he was approximately 7 or 8 years old. Modified football pants: Ed cut slits in Christian’s pants to improve knee mobility while running. Game-day IVs: Christian recalled that during high school, his father would pick him up during a Friday free period to receive an IV before games. Constant competition: Christian and his three brothers regularly competed in backyard football, basketball, and other sports.

Christian has credited his father’s approach with helping develop his work ethic and understanding of football. However, his parents also encouraged participation in multiple sports rather than specializing exclusively in football.
